thread:
tara: quick drop-in with the SpringTide-v1 embed onboarding results. did fp16, int8pc, and an int6pc exploratory run on two holdouts (wiki-qa small + short-queries). pasting key notes/questions for triage.

tara: TL;DR: int8pc ~par with fp16 on wiki-qa r@5/r@10. short-query holdout shows r@1 regression ~4.2pp for int8pc; int6pc recovers a little but also costs more of a norm shift.

lucas: ugh. which eval split and infra?

tara: wiki-qa (12k), shorthold (4k, mean tokens=3.9). runtime: x86 encoder + runtime-int8pc kernels. batch 768, max_len 64. eval command: 
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model springtide-v1 --quant int8_pc --datasets wiki_qa,shorthold --batch 768 --metric recall_at_k
```

priya: raw numbers pls. quick table.

tara: key rows (rounded):
```
model               dataset          r@1    r@5    r@10
springtide-fp16     wiki_qa          0.703  0.871  0.902
springtide-int8pc   wiki_qa          0.699  0.868  0.900
springtide-fp16     shorthold        0.641  0.812  0.845
springtide-int8pc   shorthold        0.599  0.808  0.843
springtide-int6pc   shorthold        0.614  0.809  0.844
```

tara: note int6pc improves r@1 vs int8pc but still below fp16; r@5 stable across quant levels.

anil: any metric beyond recall? silhouette? cosine-gap?

tara: did quick diagnostics: cosine_gap (top1-top2) median on shorthold: fp16=0.165, int8pc=0.078, int6pc=0.11. mean l2 norm shift small (~0.03) but distribution tail larger for int8pc.

lucas: examples of flips?

tara: selected failures where fp16 rank1 != int8pc rank1:
```
q1: \"restart vpn\"    fp16_top=A (cos=0.81)  int8pc_top=B (cos=0.66)
q2: \"pricing\"        fp16_top=C (cos=0.78)  int8pc_top=C (cos=0.76)
q3: \"refund policy\"  fp16_top=D (cos=0.69)  int8pc_top=E (cos=0.58)
```

priya: short/low-context queries again. could padding or accumulation order be amplifying error for small seqs?

tara: i profiled kernels: accumulation path for seq_len<=6 uses a different block reducer with fewer FP intermediates. forcing min_pad=8 in the encoder reduced r@1 gap by ~1.5pp for int8pc. so padding helps but is a perf/cost trade.

anil: good catch. options? pad-to-8 runtime tweak, route low-confidence short queries to fp16, or invest in per-cluster quant calibration.

lucas: what about a confidence rule (cosine_gap<0.12 and tokens<=5) fallback to fp16? cost sim?

tara: quick sim: shorthold-like traffic ~11% of production. routing those to fp16 yields ~7% cost increase overall but restores ~2.9pp r@1 globally in expected traffic. pad-to-8 adds ~5% latency for small requests but no cost delta.

priya: can we try hybrid: pad-to-8 + int6pc for short queries? or run a small A/B: baseline vs pad8 vs routing.

tara: plan:
1) run three-arm eval (baseline int8pc, int8pc+pad8, int6pc+pad8) on full holdouts (ETA 6h).
2) collect top-100 changed hits for human spot-check.
3) implement quick rollout rule draft: if tokens<=5 and cosine_gap<0.12 -> route to fp16.

anil: tagging infra and runtime to confirm pad-to-8 operational impact @infra-team.

devops-bot: scheduled job emb-eval-4300123460-three-arm (status: queued)

lucas: ok. thanks tara. please drop results CSV and add the checklist to ML-ONB-1011. i'll take human eval.

priya: also add a note to look for class-wise skew (some intents hit more). might be fixable by per-intent calibration.

tara: will do. leaving ticket in triage, will sync in embed-standup tomorrow. :seedling:
